text.p: Ameritech Corp's spending to modernize and expand its communications infrastructure increased 19 percent in 1996, the company said in a report to the Illinois Commerce Commission.
It said it is ahead of schedule toward fulfilling a pledge made to the ICC to spend at least $3 billion on network improvements over five years, beginning in 1995.

The report shows that Ameritech companies -- including the basic telecommunications business, cellular land paging services and subsidiaries for cable television and long distance -- spent $902 million on their Illinois network in 1996 compared with $761 million in 1995.

Ameritech said the increase was due mainly to keeping pace with an anticipating growth in the use of basic telephone service, the Internet, fax machines and high-speed data and video services and to improving network reliability.
Spending on growth and service continuity increased over 50 percent last year compared with 1995, to $508 million from $335 million, the communications company said.
Total spending on the basic telecommunications network advanced to $755 million from $598 million, Ameritech said.
